HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of frequent watery diarrhoea, currently 5–6 episodes/day.  
• Onset/Progression: Began abruptly 3 days ago with two episodes of vomiting; vomiting resolved, diarrhoea persists.  
• Associated symptoms: Subjective low-grade fever on day 1 (now afebrile), marked weakness, feeling dehydrated, poor oral intake, reduced appetite.  
• Negative symptoms: No visible blood or mucus in stool, no abdominal pain/cramping, no headache, no myalgia.  
• Triggers/Exposure: No recalled suspicious food, travel, or sick contacts.  
• Previous similar episodes: None reported.  
• Social/Functional impact: Missed last 3 days of work (software engineer).

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – mild, intermittent.  
• Medications: Salbutamol (blue) inhaler PRN – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father – hypertension, died of colorectal cancer at age ~58; Mother – type 2 diabetes.  
• Social: Lives alone, non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially/infrequently.

Physical Examination:
(Telephone consultation – no direct exam)  
• General: Patient appears weak by history; alert and oriented (by conversation).  
• Vitals, abdominal exam, hydration status: Not recorded.

Impression:
Acute self-limited gastroenteritis, most likely viral.  
DDx consistent with presentation:  
1. Viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood – abrupt onset vomiting then watery diarrhoea, 3-day course, no red-flag features).  
2. Food-borne bacterial gastroenteritis (medium likelihood – similar course but less supportive evidence).

Management Plan:
• Hydration: Encourage liberal clear fluids; advised oral rehydration solution (brand name Dioralyte).  
• Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol as needed for fever or malaise (dose not specified).  
• Activity: Remain off work until at least 24–48 h diarrhoea-free.  
• Monitoring: If symptoms persist beyond 1 week, worsen, or if blood appears in stool, return for in-person assessment.  
• Follow-up: Telephone or clinic review next week if not improved.

Patient Summary:
A 48-year-old man with mild asthma presents via telehealth with a 3-day course of watery diarrhoea following brief vomiting. No red-flag features. Clinical picture favours viral gastroenteritis. Supportive care and oral rehydration advised, with safety-net follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
• Drink plenty of fluids plus Dioralyte to replace salts.  
• Use paracetamol only if fever or aches occur.  
• Do not return to work until diarrhoea has stopped for 24–48 h.

Next Steps:
• Re-evaluate if symptoms persist >7 days or any warning signs (blood in stool, high fever, severe abdominal pain).  
• Consider stool testing and physical examination at follow-up if not improving.
